analysis: Examined StandaloneServer.swift BASE lines 588–1779: shutdown joins, native/GLM retention on unproven retirement, release-before-cache-clear ordering, KV shrink/build/restore accounting, idle eviction rechecks, acquisition reservations, tokenizer/catalog exposure, and weight-hash normalization. These provide context for TB-007, T-028/T-029/T-041 and model-integrity threats T-012/T-027; no changed behavior occurs within these two source excerpts according to the complete range map. The bounded patch at BASE 1964–1971 shows managed GLM loads replacing standalone pre-load hashing with a loader-verified digest while retaining weights.recheck(); the second hunk is truncated before the replacement post-load behavior is visible. This is not sufficient evidence of an integrity regression. Integration must inspect HEAD 1964–1969 and 1999–2006 and the managed-loader digest contract: verify that every relevant manifest file is authenticated before use, the digest identifies the bytes actually loaded, identity mismatches fail closed, and the same verified identity reaches modelArtifactSHA256/cacheEligibleWeightHash (BASE 1298–1299). That matters both for malicious-operator weight substitution and T-041's model/layout cache binding, plus performance-profile identity selection. No visible change affects coordinator authorization, attestation, wire encryption, billing, or fan-helper authority; shutdown remains relevant to fan lease lifetime (BASE 600–602). The missing HEAD and loader evidence is a coverage limit, not proof that the hash replacement is safe or unsafe.
